Quantum theory

 Home Physics Branches of physics
OurBigBook.com Words: 77k Articles: 1k
Quantum theory supplies a common language for quantum mechanics, measurement in quantum mechanics, and quantum information: prepare a quantum state, transform it, and ask which experimental outcomes occur. In a finite-dimensional idealization, a pure state is a normalized vector of complex numbers. Its entries are probability amplitudes; the Born rule turns their squared magnitudes into probabilities. Between measurements, an isolated system evolves by a unitary operator, preserving its norm and inner products. A quantum circuit makes this evolution explicit as a sequence of quantum gates.
The extra information carried by quantum phases is essential. Relative quantum phases affect how probability amplitudes add when different contributions reach the same output. Their interference can enhance one outcome and cancel another. A global phase, multiplying the entire quantum state by the same complex factor of magnitude one, changes neither these relative phases nor observable predictions. The Hadamard gate below provides a small experiment in which this distinction becomes a deterministic change of output.
Quantum coherence describes this capacity to interfere relative to a specified orthonormal basis. In a density matrix, it appears in off-diagonal entries; a diagonal mixed state retains the populations but lacks that basis coherence. Thus matching the probabilities of one measurement need not match the predictions of a later experiment. Baumgratz, Cramer, and Plenio made this basis-dependent viewpoint precise in their resource framework for quantum coherence. [ref].
This makes quantum information an operational question: which distinctions can a preparation, an available unitary operator, and measurement in quantum mechanics reveal? Amplitude amplification illustrates how carefully arranged interference converts a weakly represented answer into a likely observable result. Preserving the relevant quantum coherence throughout the computation is part of the physical task. [ref].

Hadamard transform (H⊗n)

Words: 613 Articles: 8
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
The normalized Hadamard transform maps a vector indexed by binary strings through entries 2−n/2(−1)x⋅y, where the dot product is evaluated modulo two. It is its own inverse and an orthogonal transformation, hence also a unitary operator on complex input vectors. The Hadamard gate is the n=1 quantum case, and the Hadamard basis is the image of the computational basis. The Walsh-Hadamard transform gives the same tensor product construction.
For two qubits, applying one Hadamard gate to each prepares the uniform quantum superposition
H⊗2∣00⟩=21​(∣00⟩+∣01⟩+∣10⟩+∣11⟩).
(1)
Each probability amplitude is 1/2, so each computational-basis measurement outcome has probability 1/4. Applying the Hadamard transform again reconstructs ∣00⟩: signed contributions cancel at the other three outputs. Its usefulness lies in combining simple local quantum gates into an operation on exponentially many amplitudes. Extracting useful information still requires an appropriate subsequent transformation and measurement.

Fast Hadamard transform

Hadamard transform OurBigBook.com

Hadamard gate (H)

Words: 463 Articles: 4
Hadamard transform OurBigBook.com
The Hadamard gate is the unitary operator
H=2​1​(11​1−1​),H2=I,
(2)
where I is the identity operator. It maps the computational basis to the Hadamard basis:
∣0⟩↦2​∣0⟩+∣1⟩​,∣1⟩↦2​∣0⟩−∣1⟩​.
(3)
These outputs have equal computational-basis measurement probabilities, but their relative quantum phase differs. Applying another Hadamard gate sends them to different definite outputs. Calling this gate a classical coin toss would discard precisely the information that makes this possible. [ref].
Starting from ∣0⟩, compare two quantum circuits, reading matrix products from right to left:
HH∣0⟩=∣0⟩,HZH∣0⟩=∣1⟩.
(4)
Here Z is the Pauli Z gate. After the first Hadamard gate, the probability amplitudes are (1/2​,1/2​). Inserting Z changes them to (1/2​,−1/2​) without changing their squared magnitudes. At the final gate, the contributions to output zero cancel and those to output one add. Without Z, cancellation occurs at output one instead. This is controlled interference, with the quantum phase determining which answer emerges.
The same calculation works for any phase gate Pϕ​=diag(1,eiϕ):
HPϕ​H∣0⟩=21+eiϕ​∣0⟩+21−eiϕ​∣1⟩,P(1)=sin2(ϕ/2),P(0)=cos2(ϕ/2).
(5)
For example, ϕ=π/3 gives P(1)=1/4, while ϕ=π/2 gives P(1)=1/2. The output-one amplitude at ϕ=π/2 is (1−i)/2: its two complex contributions add before the Born rule is applied. A phase gate alone leaves the populations unchanged; recombination converts its relative quantum phase into observable probabilities.
If quantum decoherence completely removes the computational basis coherence between the gates, the intermediate density matrix becomes I/2. Both the phase gate and final Hadamard gate leave I/2 unchanged, so P(1)=1/2 for every ϕ. The disappearing fringe explains why preserving quantum coherence matters: it enables the gate sequence to carry phase information into the final measurement.

Hadamard interchange of Y eigenstates (H∣±i⟩=e±iπ/4∣∓i⟩)

Words: 45
Hadamard gate OurBigBook.com
For ∣±i⟩=(∣0⟩±i∣1⟩)/2​, direct matrix multiplication by the Hadamard gate gives coefficients (1±i,1∓i)/2, proving the displayed identities. This exchanges the two Pauli eigenstates of the Pauli Y gate and agrees with HYH=−Y. The phases in the formula are global phases for each separate state; the relative phase inside each state is essential.

Hadamard-phase-Hadamard qubit rotation (HPα​H=eiα/2e−iασx​/2)

Words: 51
Hadamard gate OurBigBook.com
For Pα​=diag(1,eiα), conjugation by the Hadamard gate turns a relative quantum phase into an x-axis Bloch vector rotation. In the convention ρ=(I+P⋅σ)/2, the map is (Px​,Py​,Pz​)↦(Px​,Py​cosα−Pz​sinα,Py​sinα+Pz​cosα). An x-polarized input is unchanged, whereas a z-polarized input gives a sinusoidal population difference. A maximally mixed input remains maximally mixed under every unitary time evolution.

Photon-number reference for a Hadamard gate (rk​=1−1/k,sk​=max(k−2,0)/k)

Words: 95
Hadamard gate OurBigBook.com
A flat reference over k adjacent Fock states has overlap rk​ with a one-photon shift and sk​ with a two-photon shift. These overlaps, obtained by counting shared number states, determine the reduced qubit channel of a number-conserving Hadamard interaction. For k≥2, its squared fidelity with the desired pure output is 1−(1+xz)/(2k) for input Bloch vector (x,y,z). Its worst-case infidelity is 3/(4k) because ∣xz∣≤1/2. At k=1 the two-shift overlap is zero, not −1, and the fidelity is 1/2+(y2−xz)/4. Broad coherent number support, rather than merely a large fixed photon number, suppresses distinguishability of the outgoing field states.

Quantum fluctuation (⟨(O−⟨O⟩)2⟩)

Words: 78 Articles: 1
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
A quantum fluctuation is a nonzero variance of an observable in a quantum state, even when its mean vanishes. A vacuum field mode has such zero-point variance. In an inflationary background, the expanding geometry transfers short-wavelength vacuum field fluctuations into primordial perturbations as their wavelengths cross the Hubble radius.

Vacuum fluctuation

Words: 34
Quantum fluctuation OurBigBook.com
A vacuum fluctuation is a nonzero quantum variance in a vacuum state. For a single electromagnetic normal mode, dimensionless optical quadratures a+a† and −i(a−a†) have zero means and unit variances in the vacuum state, despite zero photon number. The mode's zero-point energy is ℏω/2.

Amplitude amplification

Words: 738 Articles: 7
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
Amplitude amplification increases the probability of obtaining an answer accepted by a specified Boolean function. It requires a coherent preparation A, its inverse, and a marked-state phase oracle that negates accepted components. Alternating that sign change with a reflection operator about the prepared state directs interference toward the accepted subspace. Brassard, Høyer, Mosca, and Tapp developed the general framework, extending Grover's algorithm beyond a uniform quantum superposition. [ref].
If a normalized quantum state has good amplitude sinθ, the product of the reflection in the bad axis and the reflection in the state line rotates its good-bad plane by 2θ. After k iterations the good probability is
sin2((2k+1)θ),
(9)
so O(1/sinθ) iterations raise a small good amplitude close to one. Success subsequently oscillates, making the stopping time part of the algorithm.
Compute the exact Grover search on four entries directly. Order the computational basis as 00,01,10,11 and mark 11. The Hadamard transform prepares amplitudes (1/2,1/2,1/2,1/2). The marked-state phase oracle changes these to (1/2,1/2,1/2,−1/2), whose arithmetic mean is a=1/4. The Grover diffusion operator performs inversion about the mean:
ax​⟼2a−ax​,(21​,21​,21​,−21​)⟼(0,0,0,1).
(10)
The three unmarked amplitudes become 1/2−1/2=0, while the marked amplitude becomes 1/2−(−1/2)=1. All three stages have squared norm one. Here sinθ=1/2, so θ=π/6 and one iteration gives sin2(3θ)=1, agreeing with the explicit calculation.
Grover's original search paper was submitted on 29 May 1996; its algorithm combines selective sign changes with inversion about the mean. The example exposes the beauty of that construction: a change initially invisible to computational-basis measurement becomes complete cancellation of every wrong answer. [ref].
The marked-state phase oracle is an assumed operation, whose implementation cost must be counted. Computational-basis measurement yields a candidate label, here 11; using it to retrieve a record requires the relevant data access. Preparing a quantum superposition does not make all its entries available as classical outputs. The improvement concerns the number of oracle queries needed to obtain an accepted label.

Nearest-integer stopping for amplitude amplification (r=⌊π/(4θ)⌋,sin2θ=p)

Words: 49
Amplitude amplification OurBigBook.com
For known initial success probability p∈(0,1), this choice of iteration count ensures ∣(2r+1)θ−π/2∣≤θ. Hence the success probability after amplitude amplification is at least cos2θ=1−p. Counting initial state preparation and the forward and inverse preparation in each iterate gives 2r+1 preparation-unitary applications, asymptotic to π/(2p​) as p→0.

Two-dimensional matrix for phase amplitude amplification (Q=−[I+(eiϕ−1)∣ψ⟩⟨ψ∣]diag(eiθ,1))

Words: 71
Amplitude amplification OurBigBook.com
If the state-preparation unitary sends ∣0⟩ to ∣ψ⟩=sinχ∣g⟩+cosχ∣b⟩, use the orthonormal good/bad basis. The marked-space phase is diagonal there, and conjugating a phase on ∣0⟩ gives the rank-one phase in the displayed formula. Their product is unitary. An arbitrary preparation unitary not sending zero to this state need not preserve this particular two-dimensional subspace. Matrices in unnormalized good/bad vectors must not be described as unitary in the ordinary Euclidean inner product.

Exact amplitude amplification

Words: 271 Articles: 3
Amplitude amplification OurBigBook.com
If the initial good amplitude p=sinθ is known, an ancillary qubit can reduce it to sinθ′=pc with θ′=π/(4k+2) and 0<c≤1. After k ordinary amplitude-amplification iterations the good amplitude is sin((2k+1)θ′)=1, so the target state is prepared exactly.

One-step exact Grover search with a quarter of the inputs marked (r=41​⇒Pmarked​=1)

Words: 90
Exact amplitude amplification OurBigBook.com
Start from ∣s⟩=N−1/2∑x​∣x⟩, negate amplitudes at marked indices, and apply 2∣s⟩⟨s∣−I. If the marked fraction is r, the oracle-state mean amplitude is (1−2r)/N​. Inversion about the mean therefore gives amplitudes (1−4r)/N​ on unmarked indices and (3−4r)/N​ on marked ones. The marked success probability is r(3−4r)2. At r=1/4 it is exactly one: unmarked amplitudes vanish and each marked amplitude is 2/N​. The output is uniform among the N/4 marked indices. This is an exact special case of Grover's algorithm, using one phase oracle call under the stated promise.

Known-state success dilution for exact amplitude amplification (p∗​=sin2[π/(4j+2)]≤p)

Words: 101
Exact amplitude amplification OurBigBook.com
For known good probability p=sin2θ, choose j=⌈π/(4θ)−1/2⌉. A known reversible preparation of one state with good probability p∗​ permits j ordinary amplitude amplification iterations to reach the good subspace exactly. With ancillary marking access, prepare a flag with one-probability q=p∗​/p and define joint success as good data and flag one. Reflection about the prepared product state is known, while the joint phase test requires a controlled marking oracle or a computed Boolean output. This changes the success projector and enlarges the state space; it does not evade the obstruction to uniform probability lowering by a unitary. Query costs of preparation, its inverse and marking must all be counted.

Phase-matched amplitude amplification

Words: 40
Exact amplitude amplification OurBigBook.com
Phase-matched amplitude amplification replaces the two sign-flip reflections by selective phase rotations. Choosing their phases from the known initial overlap can rotate the state exactly onto the target even when an integer number of ordinary Grover rotations would overshoot it.

Geometric amplitude-amplification schedule

Words: 26
Amplitude amplification OurBigBook.com
A geometric amplitude-amplification schedule tries iteration counts 1,2,4,8,… when the initial good amplitude is unknown. It reaches the unknown optimal scale with only a geometric-series overhead.

Reflection operator

For a unit vector ∣ψ⟩, the reflection I−2∣ψ⟩⟨ψ∣ negates the component parallel to ∣ψ⟩ and fixes its orthogonal complement.

Projector phase rotation (e−iθP=I+(e−iθ−1)P)

Words: 54
Reflection operator OurBigBook.com
For an orthogonal projection, Pk=P for k≥1. Summing the exponential series proves the displayed identity. At θ=π, the operator is I−2P, which changes the sign on the range and fixes its orthogonal complement. In Grover search algorithm, the marked-state reflection and the uniform-state reflection compose to the search iterate up to an irrelevant global phase.

Selective phase rotation

Words: 63
Reflection operator OurBigBook.com
For a unit vector ∣ψ⟩ and real ϕ,
Rψϕ​=I−(1−eiϕ)∣ψ⟩⟨ψ∣
(11)
multiplies the component parallel to ∣ψ⟩ by eiϕ and fixes its orthogonal complement. The case ϕ=π is a reflection operator.
A reflection operator is a unitary involution that changes sign on one orthogonal subspace and fixes its orthogonal complement. For a unit vector ∣ψ⟩, I−2∣ψ⟩⟨ψ∣ reflects in the hyperplane perpendicular to ∣ψ⟩.

Words: 2k Articles: 15
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
The Robertson uncertainty principle bounds the product of the standard deviations of two observables in the same quantum state. For a normalized pure state ∣ψ⟩ and self-adjoint operators A,B, write their expectation values and variances as
⟨A⟩=⟨ψ∣A∣ψ⟩,(ΔA)2=∥(A−⟨A⟩I)ψ∥2=⟨A2⟩−⟨A⟩2,

and similarly for B, where I is the identity operator. The quantum uncertainties ΔA,ΔB then obey
ΔAΔB≥21​∣⟨[A,B]⟩∣,[A,B]=AB−BA.
(33)
Here [A,B] is the commutator, and every expectation value is taken in the same ∣ψ⟩. These standard deviations describe the outcome spreads when A and B are measured on separate ensembles prepared in that same quantum state. They are not instrument errors or the change caused by a preceding measurement in quantum mechanics. The definition and bound are developed in Barton Zwiebach, Uncertainty Principle and Compatible Observables, 2013, §§1–2.
For unbounded self-adjoint operators, the operator domains matter. Assume ψ∈D(A)∩D(B), so that both second moments are finite; ⟨A2⟩ here means the second moment of the measured probability distribution, equal to ∥Aψ∥2, even if A2ψ is undefined. To use the displayed operator commutator, also assume ψ∈D(AB)∩D(BA). Without these product-domain assumptions, the always meaningful version on D(A)∩D(B) uses ∣Im⟨Aψ∣Bψ⟩∣ as its right-hand side. These qualifications prevent a formal commutator identity from being applied to an inadmissible quantum state.
The brief proof is Cauchy-Schwarz inequality applied to u=(A−⟨A⟩I)ψ and v=(B−⟨B⟩I)ψ:
ΔAΔB=∥u∥∥v∥≥∣⟨u∣v⟩∣≥∣Im⟨u∣v⟩∣=21​∣⟨[A,B]⟩∣.
(34)
The final equality uses self-adjointness and the product-domain assumptions. Thus a geometric statement about inner products becomes a constraint on experimental spreads. For nonzero ΔA,ΔB, equality requires u,v to be proportional with a purely imaginary proportionality factor; the equality case of the Heisenberg uncertainty relation turns this condition into a Gaussian wave packet.
The bound is useful because computing a single commutator and its expectation value can constrain two entire outcome distributions. Its right-hand side depends on the quantum state: the spin uncertainty state dependence example gives both a positive saturated bound and a zero bound for the same noncommuting observables. Robertson's paper, titled "The Uncertainty Principle", appeared on 1 July 1929 in Physical Review, volume 34, starting at page 163. [ref].

The mean-dependent contributions are nonnegative. The Gaussian eigenstate for a quadratic potential with σ2=ℏ/(2mω) and zero means reaches this ground state energy. This is why the tradeoff is more than a limitation on preparation: it predicts an unavoidable positive minimum energy.
Heisenberg's original article appeared in March 1927 as "Über den anschaulichen Inhalt der quantentheoretischen Kinematik und Mechanik", Zeitschrift für Physik 43, pp. 172–198. Its abstract discusses simultaneous imprecision of canonically conjugate quantities and explanatory thought experiments. The precise standard deviation formulation here distinguishes preparation spreads from a slogan about measurement disturbance. [ref].

Preparation uncertainty

Words: 130
Heisenberg uncertainty relation OurBigBook.com
Preparation uncertainty describes the outcome spread intrinsic to a specified quantum state preparation. Operationally, prepare many copies of the same quantum state, measure position on one group and momentum on another, and estimate the two variances. Ideal measurements still have the spreads predicted by the Born rule. No earlier position measurement need occur in the momentum group. The Heisenberg uncertainty relation constrains these two distributions belonging to the same preparation.
Measurement backaction concerns how a particular measurement in quantum mechanics changes a quantum state. Instrument resolution concerns how its reported outcomes relate to the intended observable. Those questions require a model of the instrument and its interaction with the system. Substituting an instrument error and an induced change for Δx and Δp in the Heisenberg uncertainty relation does not follow from its proof. The practical value of preparation uncertainty is that it bounds achievable input spreads before any such instrument model is chosen.

Heisenberg's microscope

Words: 305
Heisenberg uncertainty relation OurBigBook.com
Heisenberg's microscope is a thought experiment, not a report of a performed measurement. In Werner Heisenberg's Nobel lecture, The development of quantum mechanics, delivered on 11 December 1933, the imagined electron is illuminated with very short-wavelength light and observed through a high-resolution microscope. A scattered photon entering the observer's eye would, through Compton scattering, eject the electron from its original path. The passage challenges a classical trajectory picture; its microscope is hypothetical. The lecture date is 1933 even though the award is the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1932.[ref]
The following idealized geometry makes the tradeoff visible. Let the collected light have wavelength λ and let the microscope objective accept outgoing directions within a half-angle α about the vertical axis. Take x transverse to that axis and hold the incoming photon momentum fixed. A diffraction-limited estimate of transverse resolution has scale δx∼λ/sinα. The unobserved outgoing direction admits transverse photon momentum components between approximately −(h/λ)sinα and +(h/λ)sinα, neglecting the angular variation of the scattered wavelength. By conservation of momentum, uncertainty in that component leaves uncertainty in the transverse recoil of the electron:
δpx​∼λh​sinα,δxδpx​∼h.
(44)
Here h=2πℏ is the Planck constant; the two δ symbols denote heuristic resolution and recoil scales, not the standard deviations in the Heisenberg uncertainty relation. Increasing the acceptance angle improves the estimated resolution while broadening the allowed recoil range. Numerical factors depend on the resolution criterion and angular distribution; this scaling argument cannot supply the sharp constant ℏ/2.
The thought experiment makes the interaction needed to obtain an image memorable. The preparation uncertainty theorem has broader use: it applies to the prepared quantum state even when the two observables are measured on separate copies. No claim that Werner Heisenberg built this gamma ray apparatus is needed to understand either argument.

Lieb-Robinson interaction-chain expansion

Words: 53
Lieb-Robinson bound OurBigBook.com
Iterating the integral commutator inequality gives ordered interaction chains with factors (2∣t∣)n/n!. A per-site interaction weight at most se−μ bounds each successive chain extension by kse−μ. No chain shorter than the interaction distance connects separated supports. Reversing chains supplies the smaller support prefactor, producing the Lieb-Robinson bound. Overlapping supports require retaining the equal-time commutator term.

Interaction distance (d(X,Y))

Words: 66
Lieb-Robinson bound OurBigBook.com
The interaction distance between disjoint supports can count the minimum number of interacting hyperedges in a chain connecting them. Overlapping supports have distance zero in the usual support convention. Distances between interaction terms can instead assign shell zero only to the central term and positive shells to distinct terms. The convention must be specified when using a truncated neighborhood Hamiltonian: ordinary zero support distance includes distinct overlapping terms.

A Lieb-Robinson bound on commutators with arbitrary complement-supported unitaries then bounds the approximation error without summing over sites. For a bound proportional to e−μd(e2kst−1), choosing v=4ks/μ gives an error at most μvt∣X∣∥AX​∥e−μl/2 outside radius vt+l.

Finite-depth local quantum circuit

Words: 132 Articles: 2
Lieb-Robinson bound OurBigBook.com
A depth-D circuit of gates with range at most r expands the support of a local observable by at most rD. States connected by a depth bounded independently of system size are regarded as belonging to the same short-range-entangled phase when no required symmetry is violated.

Backward light cone of a local quantum circuit

Words: 42
Finite-depth local quantum circuit OurBigBook.com
The backward light cone of an output observable is the set of input degrees of freedom that can influence it. In a depth-D circuit with gate range at most r, it lies within distance rD of the observable's output support.

GHZ-state circuit-depth lower bound

Words: 42
Finite-depth local quantum circuit OurBigBook.com
The GHZ state has nonzero connected correlations between arbitrarily distant sites. A local circuit starting from a product state can create such a correlation only when the two backward light cones overlap, giving depth at least proportional to the system's linear size.

The coordinate Gram matrix is S=(1a​a1​) and G†SG=S. With a=sint, its eigenvalues are e±2it. Applied r times to ∣s⟩, it gives marked-state success sin2((2r+1)t). In these coordinates the overlap with the marked state is the first coefficient plus a times the second; it is not generally the first coefficient alone.

For 0<χ≤π/4, the first crossing of one half is the displayed integer, since the rounded angle stays between π/4 and 3π/4. With sin2χ=m/N≪1 this is asymptotic to (π/8)N/m​. Marked density under a permutation (p=K/N)

Grover's algorithm OurBigBook.com
For a permutation f of an N-element set and a known marked output subset of size K, exactly K inputs have marked outputs. The uniform quantum superposition thus has good probability K/N, independent of which permutation the oracle represents. This allows a known-angle amplitude amplification schedule without counting unknown preimages.

Permutation-preimage quantum search (O(N/K​))

Words: 54
Marked density under a permutation OurBigBook.com
To find an input of a permutation whose output lies in a known K-element subset, compute the output, apply its marked-state phase oracle, and use uncomputation. A modular-addition quantum oracle costs two forward queries per marked reflection, because modular-oracle inversion by negation supplies its inverse. Amplitude amplification then uses O(N/K​) queries for fixed success probability. Positive-square outputs have K=⌊N−1​⌋ and hence query cost O(N1/4).

Known-subset Grover search (O(∣B∣/k​))

Words: 181 Articles: 1
Grover's algorithm OurBigBook.com
For a known finite set B, prepare the uniform superposition state ∣sB​⟩ and implement its reflection operator 2∣sB​⟩⟨sB​∣−I. If exactly k basis states in B are marked, the same two-dimensional Grover rotation angle argument uses O(∣B∣/k​) phase queries. Preparation and reflection are known operations with no calls to the unknown predicate. Their gate cost must be accounted for separately. The success guarantee requires k>0, and choosing the optimal iteration number uses a known k.

Clean subset superposition preparation (∣0n0m⟩⟼∣ψA​⟩∣0m⟩)

Words: 110
Known-subset Grover search OurBigBook.com
Suppose a known list of 2m distinct n-bit strings aj​ is available and computational basis transpositions on n+m qubits have polynomial-size implementations. Start with the uniform superposition state of index labels j, leaving the data zero. First swap ∣0n,j⟩ with ∣aj​,j⟩ for each nonzero aj​. Next, for each j=0, swap ∣aj​,j⟩ with ∣aj​,0m⟩. Distinct index labels separate the first-stage pairs, and distinct data strings separate the second-stage pairs. Thus no later transposition disturbs an earlier term. At most 2m+1−1 transpositions prepare the uniform data state and return the quantum ancilla to zero. For m=O(logn) the quantum circuit has polynomial size. This assumes the list is available; a membership predicate alone does not supply it.

Deutsch algorithm

Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm OurBigBook.com
The one-input Deutsch algorithm determines whether a Boolean function is constant or balanced using one Boolean quantum oracle call. Initialize the input qubit in ∣+⟩ and the answer qubit in ∣−⟩. Quantum phase kickback changes the input to (−1)f(0)(∣0⟩+(−1)f(0)⊕f(1)∣1⟩)/2​. A Hadamard gate and computational-basis measurement therefore return the parity f(0)⊕f(1) with certainty.

Deutsch algorithm OurBigBook.com
If the input qubit of the Deutsch algorithm acquires conditional environment states with overlap ⟨e0​∣e1​⟩=veiα between its two Hadamard gates, its fixed zero-for-constant, one-for-balanced rule succeeds with probability (1+vcosα)/2. A known phase can be compensated before the last Hadamard gate, raising the success probability to (1+v)/2. An orthogonal pair of environment states gives v=0 and destroys all information in the input qubit about the answer; unit overlap modulus preserves coherence up to a known phase.

For an even-length Boolean string, one phase query followed by a known unitary extension can produce a zero-pair outcome with amplitude proportional to the zero-minus-one imbalance, or an index pair with amplitude proportional to the difference of their phase signs. A zero-pair observation certifies nonbalance. Every nonzero pair has opposite bits, so deleting it preserves the imbalance and allows recursion on two fewer indices. Ending with an empty list certifies balance. This quantum circuit is exact on all inputs and uses at most half the original length in queries, even without the constant-or-balanced promise.

BB84

Words: 137 Articles: 2
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
The BB84 protocol encodes random classical bits in independently chosen computational and Hadamard bases. Sender and receiver publicly compare bases and retain only positions where their bases agree; disturbance of a test sample detects eavesdropping.

BB84 intercept-resend error rate (Q=q/4)

Words: 66
BB84 OurBigBook.com
In ideal BB84 with uniform independent basis choices, intercepting a fraction q of signals, measuring in a random protocol basis and resending that result introduces sifted-key bit error rate q/4. Conditional on a retained position, the attacker chose the wrong basis with probability 1/2; then the receiver disagrees with the original bit with probability 1/2. The calculation describes one particular attack and does not establish general security.

Bit error rate (BER)

Words: 36

The bit error rate is the fraction, or probability, of transmitted or retained bits that differ between sender and receiver. In quantum key distribution, an unexpectedly high bit error rate reveals channel noise or possible eavesdropping.

Variational method (E0​≤Eψ​)

Words: 2k Articles: 16
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
The variational method estimates the lowest energy of a Quantum Hamiltonian by choosing a trial wavefunction, evaluating its energy, and optimizing the trial parameters. It uses the quantum variational principle, the Rayleigh-Ritz variational principle expressed for quantum states. Let H be a self-adjoint operator bounded below, and define E0​=infσ(H), the bottom of its spectrum. Every normalized admissible trial quantum state satisfies
Eψ​≥E0​,∥ψ∥=1.
(71)
When E0​ is an energy eigenvalue, it is the ground-state energy; equality holds precisely for a quantum state in the ground-state subspace. Otherwise the bottom of the spectrum need not be attained by any normalizable wavefunction.
Admissible means finite form energy. Choose a real b≤E0​ and use the shifted quadratic form of a positive quantum Hamiltonian:
Q(H)=D((H−bI)1/2),qH​[ψ]=∥(H−bI)1/2ψ∥2+b∥ψ∥2,Eψ​=qH​[ψ].
(72)
The form domain Q(H) is independent of this choice of b and can be larger than the operator domain D(H). For ψ∈D(H), Eψ​=⟨ψ,Hψ⟩ is the usual expectation value; for nonzero unnormalized trials, divide qH​[ψ] by ∥ψ∥2 to get the form version of the Rayleigh quotient. See the quantum variational principle for the general domain justification.
Thus each trial energy is an upper bound on E0​, and minimizing within a trial family improves that upper bound. It is not a lower bound on E0​. The Gaussian variational energy for the harmonic oscillator reaches E0​=1/2 because its family contains an exact ground state. The exact variational solution in a two-level system makes the equality condition visible as vanishing excited-state probability amplitude.
The method is useful when solving the Schrödinger equation exactly is difficult but integrals of a trial wavefunction are tractable. Enlarging a trial family cannot increase its optimal energy, although an optimum need not be attained. The beauty is that even an imperfect trial gives a rigorous bound, provided its form energy is computed exactly: numerical integration errors require separate control. The Gaussian variational estimate for a solvable sextic potential provides an existing example beyond a quantum harmonic oscillator.
A short proof explains the direction. With a complete orthonormal eigenbasis of energy eigenstates, write ψ=∑n​cn​ϕn​, where Hϕn​=En​ϕn​ and ∑n​∣cn​∣2=1. Then
Eψ​−E0​=∑n​∣cn​∣2(En​−E0​)≥0.
(73)
This is a weighted mean of nonnegative energy differences; equality requires every occupied energy eigenstate to have energy E0​. [ref]. For continuous spectrum, the spectral theorem replaces the sum by an integral against the scalar spectral measure of ψ, with the same nonnegative integrand. This proves the bound without assuming an orthonormal eigenbasis exists.
The historical setting predates quantum mechanics: Rayleigh's The Theory of Sound, volume I, appeared in 1877, and Ritz's paper on solving variational problems of mathematical physics appeared in volume 135 of Crelle's journal, catalogued by its publisher as 1909, pp. 1–61. These are original works associated with the Rayleigh-Ritz method; the dates here identify the publications rather than assert priority. [ref]; [ref].

An even one-dimensional confining potential preserves even and odd parity. Domain assumptions in singular-potential virial arguments

Fall to the centre for a supercritical inverse-power potential OurBigBook.com
For the formal one-dimensional operator H=p2/(2m)−a∣x∣−p with a>0 and p>2, take a smooth normalized test function supported away from the origin. Its normalized dilation ψλ​(x)=λ​ψ(λx) has
E(λ)=λ2T+λpU,T>0,U<0.
(82)
As λ→∞, this tends to minus infinity. Thus the unregularized expression has fall to the centre for a supercritical inverse-power potential and cannot define a semibounded Hamiltonian operator on a domain containing these test functions.
If a putative bound state has separately finite T,U and admits norm-preserving dilation variations inside its operator domain or energy domain, stationarity gives 2T+pU=0, hence E=(1−2/p)T>0, incompatible with a negative-energy bound state below the zero continuum threshold. For a putative ground state, the second scaling derivative is 2(2−p)T<0, also incompatible with a minimum. The argument's finite-energy and domain assumptions are essential: it proves absence of a stable ground state and excludes bound states to which this ordinary virial calculation applies. An unqualified assertion about all formal square-integrable solutions at the singular origin needs a specified self-adjoint realization; adding a short-distance cutoff changes the problem.

Exact variational solution in a two-level system (E(θ)=2sin2θ)

Words: 187 Articles: 1
Variational method OurBigBook.com
In a two-level system, let the Hamiltonian operator have matrix H=diag(0,2) in the orthonormal basis ∣0⟩,∣1⟩. The normalized real trial quantum states and their Rayleigh quotient are
∣ψθ​⟩=cosθ∣0⟩+sinθ∣1⟩,E(θ)=⟨ψθ​∣H∣ψθ​⟩=2sin2θ.
(83)
The excited-state probability amplitude is sinθ, so its probability is sin2θ. Thus E(θ)≥0=E0​, with equality if and only if the excited-state probability amplitude vanishes: θ∈πZ. The remaining quantum state is ∣0⟩ up to a global phase. At θ=π/4 the trial energy is 1; at θ=π/2 it is 2. These are upper bounds on the ground-state energy, even though neither is a minimizing trial.
The real trial family contains the ground state, so it attains the exact minimum despite not covering every complex quantum state. More generally, a family covering all normalized vectors in a two-dimensional Hilbert space gives the exact lowest eigenvalue of any Hermitian matrix by minimizing its Rayleigh quotient. For a complex trial c0​∣0⟩+c1​∣1⟩ with ∣c0​∣2+∣c1​∣2=1, the same calculation gives E=2∣c1​∣2: a relative quantum phase cannot change this diagonal Hamiltonian energy. This finite example is the weighted mean proof of the variational method with just two energy eigenstates.

GHZ game
Words: 177
GHZ theorem OurBigBook.com
A three-party nonlocal game with binary questions of even Hamming weight. Its winning output parity is half the question weight modulo two. For the four possible input triples, a hypothetical deterministic classical response would give four parity equations whose left sides cancel under exclusive or, while their right sides have odd total parity. Thus no classical strategy succeeds on every allowed triple, even with pre-shared randomness.
On the GHZ state, measure the Pauli X gate as an observable for question zero and the Pauli Y gate for question one, and encode the measured eigenvalue as (−1)x. The joint observables XXX, XYY, YXY and YYX have respective GHZ eigenvalues +1,−1,−1,−1. Their products of local outcomes enforce the required parity with certainty. The strategy uses pre-shared quantum entanglement and local measurements during the game, without communication. It realizes the GHZ theorem as an operational task. If the four questions are uniform, the best classical success is 3/4: the parity contradiction bounds it above, and the deterministic rule x=a, y=z=0 wins three triples and loses only 011. The uniformity assumption is necessary for that numerical score, not for the impossibility of worst-case certainty.

Quantum decoherence

Words: 876 Articles: 16
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
Quantum decoherence is the suppression of observable phase coherence when a system becomes entangled with unobserved environmental degrees of freedom. In a preferred basis, tracing out the environment damps off-diagonal entries of the system's reduced density matrix while leaving the corresponding populations unchanged.

Tracing out the environment multiplies detector coherences by this number while preserving the populations. Orthogonal records occur at A=π/4, but coherence returns later. For equal initial detector populations the reduced purity is (1+cos22A)/2. Thus complete reduced dephasing at one time does not imply irreversible global collapse.

Wigner's friend

Words: 69
Measurement problem OurBigBook.com
A thought experiment placing a friend's physical measurement record inside a larger isolated quantum laboratory. Conditioned on a record the friend has a definite outcome, while an external observer using universal unitary evolution can assign an entangled laboratory state. Its contrast with a collapsed mixture is an instance of the quantum measurement problem; it does not require giving consciousness a special dynamical law. Eugene Wigner used the observer-within-the-system construction to examine such tensions.

Words: 57
Measurement problem OurBigBook.com
A thought experiment correlating a microscopic quantum alternative with macroscopically distinct records, introduced by Erwin Schrödinger to sharpen the problem of applying unitary evolution to a measuring apparatus. The resulting entangled superposition and the mixture produced by selecting an outcome are different joint density operators. Quantum decoherence can make the records' reduced density operator approximately diagonal without selecting a single global component.

Preferred-basis problem

Words: 61
Measurement problem OurBigBook.com
The problem of explaining which basis represents stable measurement records. A maximally entangled quantum premeasurement state can have several equally weighted Schmidt decompositions. Choosing a different decomposition does not alter that pure state, but declaring a projection in a different basis generally changes the resulting mixture. Environment-induced pointer-basis selection supplies a dynamical account of robust records, while leaving the further question of a single realized outcome distinct.

Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
Quantum gravity seeks a theory in which gravity and quantum phenomena are described consistently.

Quantum gravity with a two-dimensional spacetime or worldsheet. In the string formulation, one sums over surface metrics and topologies with matter fields on each surface. This worldsheet theory is distinct from the target-space gravity described by the graviton in the closed-string spectrum.

Graviton

Quantum gravity OurBigBook.com
A graviton is the massless spin-two quantum of the gravitational field. It occurs in the symmetric trace-free transverse sector of the first massless closed string level.

Semiclassical gravity couples a classical spacetime metric to quantum matter. In its simplest expectation-value form, the classical gravitational field is sourced by the quantum expectation of the matter stress-energy tensor.

The semiclassical Einstein equation is
Gμν​=8πG⟨Tμν​⟩
(100)
in units with c=1. A single classical metric responds to the expectation value over all matter branches.

The Page–Geilker experiment used a quantum random decision to choose a macroscopic source-mass configuration and measured its field with a torsion balance. The observed field followed the configuration in the observed branch rather than the nearly cancelling expectation-value average predicted by the simplest no-collapse semiclassical Einstein equation.

Gravitationally induced entanglement

Words: 77 Articles: 1
Quantum gravity OurBigBook.com
When two masses occupy spatial superpositions, their branch-dependent Newtonian gravitational potential energy produces relative phases. If those phases cannot be separated into one phase for each mass, the interaction turns an initial product state into an entangled state.

Gravitationally induced entanglement OurBigBook.com
The Bose--Marletto--Vedral experiment proposes placing two nearby masses in spatial superpositions and detecting the entanglement generated by their branch-dependent gravitational phases. Under locality assumptions and in the absence of other interactions, an entangling mediator must possess incompatible observables rather than behave as a single classical local variable.

A pure quantum state is represented by a unit vector ∣ψ⟩ up to global phase, or equivalently by the rank-one density operator ∣ψ⟩⟨ψ∣.

Pure state OurBigBook.com
The Euclidean norm distance between normalized pure state vector representatives in a common Hilbert space. Its square is 2−2Re⟨ψ∣ϕ⟩. If vectors differing by a global phase are identified, minimize over that phase to obtain 2−2∣⟨ψ∣ϕ⟩∣​. This is a different distance convention from trace distance or one minus squared quantum fidelity; stating the convention is necessary when defining ε-closeness.

Pure state OurBigBook.com
For a bipartite vector ∣v⟩∈HR​⊗HA​ and a chosen orthonormal basis of R, the generally unnormalized relative state on A is obtained by the partial inner product with one basis vector. It gives the expansion ∣v⟩=∑j​∣j⟩⊗∣ηj​⟩. The squared norm of a relative state is the probability of its corresponding basis outcome when ∣v⟩ is normalized. Relative states of eigenvectors of a Choi matrix construct the columns of its Kraus operators.

Index state (∣j⟩R​)

Words: 88 Articles: 1
Relative state of a bipartite vector OurBigBook.com
An index state is a chosen orthonormal basis vector in the indexing subsystem of a relative state decomposition. It labels the corresponding partial inner product; it need not be an eigenvector of the subsystem's reduced density matrix.

Words: 55
Index state OurBigBook.com
Fix paired orthonormal bases and let ∣ϕ⟩A​=∑j​cj​∣j⟩A​. Its conjugate index vector in the other Hilbert space uses the conjugated coefficients. For the unnormalized maximally entangled state ∣Ψ⟩=∑j​∣j⟩A​∣j⟩B​, the partial inner product is (I⊗⟨ϕB∗​∣)∣Ψ⟩=∣ϕ⟩A​. Both the conjugation and the lack of normalization of Ψ matter. Applying a linear operator on the first subsystem gives the corresponding relative state of the operated vector.

Partial trace (TrB​)

Words: 230 Articles: 3
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
The partial trace over B is the linear operation characterized by
Tr[MA​TrB​(XAB​)]=Tr[(MA​⊗IB​)XAB​].
(101)
Applied to a density operator, it produces a reduced density matrix.

Partial trace in a nonorthogonal product expansion (Ψ=∑j​ξj​⊗ηj​,S1​=∑j,k​⟨ηk​,ηj​⟩∣ξj​⟩⟨ξk​∣)

Words: 103
Partial trace OurBigBook.com
The vectors need not form orthonormal bases. With the inner product linear in its second entry, expand the rank-one operator ∣Ψ⟩⟨Ψ∣ and take the trace on the second factor. This gives the displayed reduced positive operator. For every observable A on the first factor,
⟨Ψ,(A⊗I)Ψ⟩=Tr(AS1​),TrS1​=∥Ψ∥2.
(102)
Positivity also follows directly from ⟨v,S1​v⟩=∥∑j​⟨v,ξj​⟩ηj​∥2. Thus the physical density operator is S1​/∥Ψ∥2 when the nonzero source vector is not normalized. The Gram matrix of the second-factor vectors supplies the cross coefficients; replacing those coefficients by Kronecker deltas without checking orthonormality changes the subsystem state. This formula is useful when an efficient product expansion uses nonorthogonal vectors, even though the partial trace itself is basis-independent.

Words: 62
Partial trace OurBigBook.com
The partial trace of a positive operator is positive by this sum of nonnegative expectations in an orthonormal basis of the traced factor. Its trace equals the original trace, using the product orthonormal basis. Basis independence follows from Tr[(TrB​ρ)A]=Tr[ρ(A⊗I)], which uniquely determines the reduced operator. Thus reductions of density matrices remain density matrices. For a positive trace-class operator the same argument uses convergent nonnegative basis sums.

For an operator on a tensor-product Hilbert space, averaging unitary conjugations on subsystem B with normalized Haar measure gives EA​(O)=(TrB​O/dB​)⊗IB​. It fixes precisely the operators acting trivially on B and is contractive in operator norm. Writing O−UOU†=[O,U]U† converts localization error into a commutator bound.

Adiabatic theorem

Words: 143 Articles: 2
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
If a Hamiltonian changes sufficiently slowly while an eigenstate remains separated from the rest of the spectrum by a nonzero gap, evolution keeps the state in the corresponding instantaneous eigenspace up to a dynamical and geometric phase. A degenerate isolated eigenspace can undergo a unitary holonomy within itself.

Instantaneous eigenstate coupling (Amn​=⟨m(t)∣∂t​n(t)⟩)

Words: 42
Adiabatic theorem OurBigBook.com
Expanding a quantum state in instantaneous energy eigenstates separates dynamical phases from the coupling Amn​. orthonormality makes A anti-Hermitian. For distinct eigenvalues, differentiating the eigenvalue equation gives Amn​=⟨m∣H˙∣n⟩/(En​−Em​). Its off-diagonal entries drive nonadiabatic transitions; diagonal entries describe phase changes of the basis and generate the Berry phase.

Adiabatic preparation of a computational history state (τ=O(T6/ϵ))

Words: 53
Adiabatic theorem OurBigBook.com
A Hamiltonian path preserving the history subspace can be analysed using its restricted spectral gap. If this gap is Ω(T−2) and the derivative has operator norm O(1), a runtime criterion proportional to ∥H˙∥2/(ϵΔ3) permits computational history state preparation in time O(T6/ϵ). Other invariant sectors do not cause leakage from a state initialized in the history subspace.

Matrices Ai define both the completely positive map E(X)=∑i​AiX(Ai)† and an MPS. Repeatedly retaining the Kraus label i purifies the channel output into the physical MPS chain; tracing those labels recovers repeated application of E.

Matrix product state OurBigBook.com
For an MPS tensor Ai, the transfer map is the completely positive map E(X)=∑i​AiX(Ai)†. Its fixed points control normalization and local expectation values, while its subleading eigenvalues control correlation lengths.

Matrix product state OurBigBook.com
An MPS tensor is injective after blocking when products of its physical matrices span the full virtual matrix algebra.
Blocking a matrix product state

Injective matrix product state OurBigBook.com
Blocking L neighboring sites replaces their physical labels by one composite label and their tensor by the products Ai1​⋯AiL​. An MPS is injective when such products span the full virtual matrix algebra for some finite L.
Uniform matrix product state (uniform MPS)
Words: 24
Injective matrix product state OurBigBook.com
A uniform matrix product state uses the same local tensor Ai at every site. For a periodic chain its amplitudes are Tr(Ai1​⋯AiN​).

Words: 62 Articles: 1
Injective matrix product state OurBigBook.com
Two injective uniform MPS tensors generate the same states on every sufficiently long periodic chain exactly when they differ by a virtual similarity transform and an overall phase: Ai=eiθXBiX−1.

Words: 32
Fundamental theorem of matrix product states OurBigBook.com
The virtual similarity transformation Ai↦XAiX−1 leaves every periodic MPS amplitude invariant by cyclicity of the matrix trace. The fundamental theorem of matrix product states says that, up to an overall phase, this is the only ambiguity for injective uniform tensors.
Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki state (AKLT state)
Words: 181 Articles: 4
Injective matrix product state OurBigBook.com
The Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki state is an injective spin-one MPS whose virtual degrees of freedom are spin one-half. Its Z2​×Z2​ symmetry acts linearly on physical spins and projectively on the virtual spins.

Words: 76 Articles: 1
Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki state OurBigBook.com
In a Cartesian basis of the physical spin-one space, the AKLT MPS matrices are proportional to σx​,σy​,σz​. Products of two such matrices span the full virtual matrix algebra, and the two-site parent term projects onto total spin two.
Two-site support of the Pauli-matrix Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki tensor
Words: 37
Pauli-matrix representation of the Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki state OurBigBook.com
Because σi​σj​=δij​I+iεijk​σk​, the two-site image of the Pauli-matrix AKLT tensor is the direct sum of the scalar and antisymmetric subspaces, which have total spin zero and one. Its orthogonal complement is the symmetric traceless total-spin-two subspace.

Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki state OurBigBook.com
The AKLT parent Hamiltonian is H=∑j​Pj,j+1(2)​, where P(2) projects two neighboring spin-one particles onto total spin two. It is frustration free, and the periodic AKLT MPS is its unique ground state on a sufficiently long chain.
Symmetry-protected equivalence of the Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki state and cluster state
Words: 35
Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki state OurBigBook.com
After suitable blocking, the AKLT and one-dimensional cluster states realize the same nontrivial Z2​×Z2​ symmetry-protected topological phase. Their virtual symmetries carry the same nontrivial projective class and produce protected edge degrees of freedom.

Matrix product state OurBigBook.com
The entanglement spectrum is the spectrum of −logρA​, equivalently the negative logarithms of squared Schmidt coefficients. A nontrivial projective virtual symmetry can enforce degeneracies throughout this spectrum.

An MPS parent Hamiltonian is a sum of local projectors onto the orthogonal complement of the tensor's local support. The MPS is a frustration-free ground state.

Hamiltonian simulation constructs a quantum circuit approximating the time-evolution operator e−itH generated by a Hamiltonian operator H, with cost controlled by the evolution time, requested precision, and structure of H.

e−itH=∏j​e−ithj​

exactly. Approximating each fixed-size factor to error at most ε/m and applying the telescoping bound for products of operators gives total operator norm error at most ε.

Hamiltonian simulation OurBigBook.com
A local Hamiltonian is a sum of terms, each acting nontrivially on only a bounded number of subsystems.

Operator support (supp(A))

Words: 54
Local Hamiltonian OurBigBook.com
The operator support is the set of subsystems on which an operator may act nontrivially; it acts as the identity outside that set. Unitary time evolution can enlarge the support, while a Lieb-Robinson bound controls the error of replacing the evolved operator by one with smaller support. The support diameter and the number of sites in the support are different quantities.

Stoquastic Hamiltonian

Words: 38
Local Hamiltonian OurBigBook.com
A stoquastic Hamiltonian is a real Hermitian Hamiltonian operator with nonpositive off-diagonal entries in a specified basis, usually the computational basis. The property depends on that basis. Permutation matrices in a quantum circuit's propagation terms and ∣−⟩⟨−∣ input penalties give a useful family of such operators.

Spectral filtering of Hamiltonian terms (gZ​=∫w(t)eitHhZ​e−itHdt)

Words: 282 Articles: 4
Local Hamiltonian OurBigBook.com
A real nonnegative normalized filter w defines gZ​=∫w(t)eitHhZ​e−itHdt. In an energy eigenbasis, it multiplies each matrix element by w(Ei​−Ej​). A Fourier cutoff at the spectral gap removes couplings between a unique ground state and excitations. The filtered terms still sum to H, because the total Hamiltonian is unchanged by its own unitary time evolution. Each term commutes with the ground projector, but need not be minimized there.

Words: 59
Spectral filtering of Hamiltonian terms OurBigBook.com
In a telescoping local-shell decomposition, split the spectral filter integral at a time proportional to the shell distance. A Lieb-Robinson bound controls short times, while the two-sided almost-exponential spectral filter tail controls long times. Polynomial shell-weight growth then gives the displayed decay. The estimate is asymptotic at large distance; small shells retain the elementary operator-norm bound. The evenization of a nonnegative bandlimited filter can supply the two-sided tail from a one-sided existence statement.
Filtering preserves existing frustration freeness
Words: 50
Spectral filtering of Hamiltonian terms OurBigBook.com
If each local term is already minimized by the global ground state, subtract its minimum aZ​ to obtain a positive operator. Nonnegative normalized spectral filtering of Hamiltonian terms preserves positivity and leaves the ground eigenvalue aZ​ unchanged. Thus the same state minimizes every filtered term. This preserves frustration freeness but does not create it for an initially frustrated decomposition.
Commuting with a ground projector does not imply frustration freeness
Words: 56
Spectral filtering of Hamiltonian terms OurBigBook.com
The condition [gZ​,P0​]=0 makes a unique global ground state an eigenvector of every filtered term, but its termwise eigenvalues can exceed the corresponding minima. For example h12​=∣1⟩⟨1∣1​+∣0⟩⟨0∣2​ and h23​=∣1⟩⟨1∣3​+2∣1⟩⟨1∣2​ commute with their sum. Their sum is uniquely minimized by ∣000⟩, yet h12​ is lower on ∣010⟩. Filtering leaves these commuting terms unchanged, so it cannot force frustration freeness.

Words: 51
Spectral filtering of Hamiltonian terms OurBigBook.com
Filter a fixed local term using a nested sequence of neighbourhood Hamiltonians Hs​, and call the results Gs​. The differences Gs​−Gs−1​ give a shell decomposition. When H0​=hZ​ and HD​=H, normalization gives G0​=hZ​ and telescoping gives gZ​=hZ​+∑s=1D​(Gs​−Gs−1​). Individual shell terms need not commute with the full ground projector.

Local Hamiltonian OurBigBook.com
Given a polynomial list of fixed-locality Hermitian terms and thresholds a<b separated by at least an inverse polynomial, distinguish whether the minimum eigenvalue of their sum is at most a or at least b. Terms may be normalized to 0≤hj​≤I with polynomial rescaling. This promise problem is in QMA by local-energy measurement verification.
Local-energy measurement verification
Words: 65
Local Hamiltonian problem OurBigBook.com
Uniformly sample one positive local term and measure the effect hj​. The averaged energy-flag effect on a witness is H/M, where M is the number of terms. Repetition with a threshold halfway between the promised flag probabilities uses O(M2/(b−a)2) witness registers for constant error. A spectral tensor-product analysis, as in QMA parallel repetition with entangled witnesses, proves soundness against entangled witnesses. Constant-locality positive operator-valued measures are efficiently implementable using one ancilla qubit.

A diagonal Hamiltonian is diagonal in a specified product basis, usually the computational basis. Every basis state is therefore an energy eigenstate, and optimization of its diagonal entries becomes minimization of the corresponding classical cost function.

Local Hamiltonian OurBigBook.com
A quantum Hamiltonian H=∑j​hj​ with positive-semidefinite local terms is frustration free when one state minimizes every hj​ simultaneously. After shifting each local minimum to zero, that state lies in every kernel kerhj​ and has zero total energy.

Words: 157 Articles: 2
Frustration-free quantum Hamiltonian OurBigBook.com
In a nearest-neighbour frustration-free Hamiltonian chain, multiply the bond orthogonal projections in two disjoint alternating layers. The resulting product K fixes the common ground state space but contracts its orthogonal complement by a factor bounded away from one in terms of the spectral gap. A bound ∥K∣suppH​∥≤(1+Δ/2)−1/3 implies exponentially convergent powers. The product is generally neither Hermitian nor normal.

To evaluate a layered product on Ax​∣ψ0​⟩, scan the bond orthogonal projections from right to left. A projection disjoint from the current support commutes through the accumulated operator and disappears against the common ground state. Retained projections expand the support by at most one site per layer. Their product L gives a local operator LAx​ with both KrAx​∣ψ0​⟩=LAx​∣ψ0​⟩ and ⟨ψ0​∣LAx​=⟨ψ0​∣Ax​.

Combine a local projector cone in a frustration-free chain with the contraction bound from the detectability lemma. If the localized operator misses a second observable's support, their commutation and the exact ground-state bra identity convert the connected correlation function into an approximation error. The two-projection power estimate yields spatial decay rate α=31​ln(1+Δ/2) for the stated detectability contraction.

A decomposition H=∑Z​hZ​ has frustration freeness when a global ground state minimizes every term simultaneously. For finite-dimensional Hermitian terms this implies E0​(H)=∑Z​E0​(hZ​). Shifting each term by its minimum produces positive operators with a common null vector. The property depends on the decomposition, not only the total operator.
